knowledge_point.title: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Express $\cos\left(t+\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ in terms of $\sin t$ or $\cos t$.

$\cos\left(t+\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the sum formula:

$$
\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v
$$

With $u=t$ and $v=\frac{3\pi}{2}$, the exact values are $\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=0$ and $\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=-1$. Substitute and collect the terms in the requested order:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos\left(t+\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)&=\cos t\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)-\sin t\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\\
&=\cos t\cdot\left(0\right)-\sin t\cdot\left(-1\right)\\
&=\sin t.
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Express $\cos\left(x-\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ or $\cos x$.

$\cos\left(x-\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the difference formula:

$$
\cos(u-v)=\cos u\cos v+\sin u\sin v
$$

With $u=x$ and $v=\frac{3\pi}{2}$, the exact values are $\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=0$ and $\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=-1$. Substitute and collect the terms in the requested order:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos\left(x-\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)&=\cos x\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)+\sin x\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\\
&=\cos x\cdot\left(0\right)+\sin x\cdot\left(-1\right)\\
&=-\sin x.
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/problem:
Express $\cos\left(t+\pi\right)$ in terms of $\sin t$ or $\cos t$.

$\cos\left(t+\pi\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the sum formula:

$$
\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v
$$

With $u=t$ and $v=\pi$, the exact values are $\cos(\pi)=-1$ and $\sin(\pi)=0$. Substitute and collect the terms in the requested order:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos\left(t+\pi\right)&=\cos t\cos\left(\pi\right)-\sin t\sin\left(\pi\right)\\
&=\cos t\cdot\left(-1\right)-\sin t\cdot\left(0\right)\\
&=-\cos t.
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Express $\cos\left(t+2\pi\right)$ in terms of $\sin t$ or $\cos t$.

$\cos\left(t+2\pi\right)=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the sum formula:

$$
\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v
$$

With $u=t$ and $v=2\pi$, the exact values are $\cos(2\pi)=1$ and $\sin(2\pi)=0$. Substitute and collect the terms in the requested order:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\cos\left(t+2\pi\right)&=\cos t\cos\left(2\pi\right)-\sin t\sin\left(2\pi\right)\\
&=\cos t\cdot\left(1\right)-\sin t\cdot\left(0\right)\\
&=\cos t.
\end{aligned}
$$
